Non-magical Roman arena net fighter, dark ochre short tunic, worn single shoulder guard, coiled rope net in left hand and short trident in right; visibly open rope lattice, no magic. Exactly FOUR columns and FOUR rows, 16 separate complete poses of ONE SAME character. Read left to right, top to bottom. Original hand-painted digital dark fantasy. Sculpted painterly volume, broken confident contours, sharply selected silver highlights, worn dark metal and pale layered cloth. Roman culture supplies arena masonry and ordinary legion equipment; magical figures and creatures are raw original fantastical designs. Shared cool upper-left light and small contact shadows. Smooth opaque painted cloth and metal, rich physical volume, no heavy cartoon outline. Sheet aspect 1:1. Original designs only.

arguments.Prompt:
Original hand-painted digital dark fantasy game character ANIMATION SHEET on a solid uniform vivid MAGENTA #FF00FF background. Character identity, face, clothes, and equipment strictly matching Reference-1.png: a non-magical Roman arena net fighter (retiarius), wearing a dark ochre short tunic, worn single metal shoulder guard (galerus) on left shoulder, holding a short three-pronged trident in right hand and a coiled rope net with visibly open rope lattice in left hand. No magic. Painting style strictly matching Reference-2.png: sculpted painterly volume, broken confident contours, sharply selected highlights, worn dark metal, smooth opaque paint, cool upper-left lighting. Camera angle is elevated 55-degree orthographic view (isometric high angle, not eye-level). Character shown in FRONT-RIGHT three-quarter view, head and torso facing diagonally TOWARD the viewer and image RIGHT, face and front surfaces visible across all poses.

Arranged in an exact 4x4 grid of 16 separate poses of the ONE SAME character, read left to right, top to bottom:
- Row 1 (Quick flinch and recovery): Pose 1 is ready upright pose; Pose 2 is a sharp unmistakable recoil with shoulders and head pulled back by one head-width and torso bent back 25 degrees; Pose 3 is shoulders returning forward with braced bent legs; Pose 4 is upright recovered ready pose.
- Row 2 (Bigger stagger): Pose 5 is upright ready pose; Pose 6 is an abrupt backward bend of upper body; Pose 7 is deepest backward bend with arms pulled close and balance visibly lost; Pose 8 is lower body catching the weight on bent knees.
- Row 3 (Stagger recovery and collapse initiation): Pose 9 is pushing back upright, visibly struggling; Pose 10 is upright recovered pose; Pose 11 is ready upright pose; Pose 12 is legs buckling and body dropping low.
- Row 4 (Collapse to lying flat): Pose 13 is body very low leaning toward the ground; Pose 14 is torso falling sideways nearly horizontal; Pose 15 is body settled FULLY LYING on its side, head and entire torso flat on the ground; Pose 16 is body completely still FULLY LYING FLAT ON THE GROUND, horizontal resting body, legs extended or naturally folded, trident and net resting beside the body.

The final two poses (15 and 16) are fully horizontal lying on the ground, theatrical rest, intact body, no blood, no gore, no wounds, no attacker. Each cell contains exactly ONE full body at identical scale within the middle 60% of the cell. Wide clean empty vivid magenta #FF00FF gutters between cells. No borders, gridlines, labels, text, or floor textures.
